clue.text: Hardy's was a "major"

parts.note: Thomas Hardy wrote a novel whose title pairs a brass player with an army rank: the clue asks for the first half of that title

explanation.surface: A remark about some officer named Hardy holding the rank of major.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'major' hint at a title: Hardy's novel is The Trumpet-Major, so his 'major' was this kind of musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's novel The Trumpet-Major names its hero by his instrument and his rank.

clue.text: Book item of, loriner's bill

definitions.meaning: a loriner makes bits and spurs

explanation.surface: A line in a bridle-maker's account for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Old bills listed goods as 'To one bit' and so on; a loriner makes horses' bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha, and a bit-maker's invoice line reads 'To bit'.

clue.text: Expel fox from a bend of the Arun

indicators.note: a river bend twists the course, so the letters of the river's name are twisted

explanation.surface: Hunting a fox out of a loop of the Sussex river Arun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bend of' signals rearranging THE ARUN. The Arun is a river in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging a fox out of its earth is the hunting sense of this verb.

clue.text: Where three balls are held over while. little men's dances proceed

definitions.text: Where three balls are held over

parts.note: the small chess pieces, with the possessive giving the plural
informal dances, as at a village hop

explanation.surface: A scene of juggling while little people dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Three golden balls are the pawnbroker's sign; goods are held over as pledges.
explanation.definitionFit: Three golden balls hang over a pawnbroker's premises, where pledged goods are kept.

clue.text: Such as Eros of Piccadilly .Circus '

parts.note: the London statue known as Eros holds a bow, so he is a lover of archery

explanation.surface: Pointing to the famous London statue as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Piccadilly Circus is a London junction whose statue, called Eros, is an archer with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rather formal word for an archer, from Greek for lover of the bow.

clue.text: Heavenly, mutton

parts.note: the zodiac sign Aries is a male sheep in the sky

explanation.surface: Divinely good lamb for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Aries is the constellation of the male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries the constellation is a male sheep, the animal that yields mutton.

clue.text: Stick to keep, the play going

definitions.meaning: a short rod, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's
in cricket, to carry on batting, written as two words

explanation.surface: Advice to persevere so that a theatrical production does not close.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as BAT ON: a batsman who keeps the play going bats on.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor's rod is a slim stick, and continuing an innings in cricket is batting on.

clue.text: Of course a nob would be domineering

definitions.text: Of course a nob would be domineering

parts.words: Of course a nob would be domineering
parts.note: a nob is a knob, which is a boss or stud, so it would be studded with bosses; and a toff gives orders

explanation.surface: A snob remark that the upper class naturally bullies others.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'nob' as a knob: a raised knob is a boss, so it is boss-y.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering person orders others about, and studded with raised knobs is the other sense.

clue.text: Old master's drawn game

parts.note: a drawn match is a tie
polo, played on horseback

explanation.surface: An old painter's game ended in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master's' is 'Old master is'; Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter, and 'drawn' plays on drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Giambattista Tiepolo was a great Venetian painter of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: But they're a headache for educationists

definitions.text: But they're a headache for educationists

parts.words: But they're a headache for educationists
parts.note: dim pupils are a teacher's problem, and the word contains skulls, the seat of a headache

explanation.surface: Unruly children are a trial for teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'headache' joke: these dunces' skulls are part of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunces and blockheads slow to learn.

clue.text: Workers increase in polish.

parts.note: worker bees, the crossword's standard workers
to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Labourers getting more polish over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax from the honeycomb is rubbed into furniture as a shining finish.

clue.text: Man's justice may so judge wrongly?

definitions.text: Man's justice may so judge wrongly?

parts.words: Man's justice may so judge wrongly?
parts.note: on the Isle of Man the judges are called deemsters, so a Manx judge who errs would deem amiss

explanation.surface: A doubt about whether human justice can err.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose judges are deemsters; one judging wrongly would mis-deem.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge, and the prefix mis- makes it mistaken.

clue.text: Old port's revolutionary products

definitions.meaning: Tyre was an ancient Phoenician seaport, here with a possessive
wheel rims of rubber are products that revolve

explanation.surface: Goods made in an ancient harbour town that changed the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre is the Phoenician harbour city, and rubber wheel coverings go round as they roll.

clue.text: More redweed than hay in it makes it rot

parts.note: the red-flowered poppy, a weed of cornfields
a cock is a conical heap of hay, a haycock

explanation.surface: A complaint that a haystack full of weeds will spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: A haycock with more poppies than hay in it would be a poppy-cock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot in the sense of nonsense is a synonym of this word for foolish talk.

clue.text: Could be Ralph re Enid or Don Juan

indicators.note: the letters of these names could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A love triangle: Ralph writing about Enid, or a famous seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' signals rearranging RALPH RE ENID.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary seducer, a womanizer.

clue.text: Residual tree

definitions.meaning: an adjective standing for the noun: what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A tree that is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The powder left after a fire is a residue, and the same word names a timber tree of the olive family.

clue.text: Habituation to a. Christian way of speaking

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, the Christian era of dating
diction is one's manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Getting used to Christian speech habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependence formed by habit, such as on a drug.

clue.text: One way of trying to find the value of "x"

definitions.text: One way of trying to find the value of "x"

parts.words: One way of trying to find the value of "x"
parts.note: the x is the cross a voter marks, and a survey of voters tries to measure them

explanation.surface: Solving for x in an algebra lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: The algebraic 'x' is really the cross on a ballot; canvassing voters estimates where those crosses will go.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey canvassing public views tries to forecast how ballots will be marked.

clue.text: Tench-size: sort of German philosopher

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish-sized German thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' signals rearranging TENCH-SIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was the German author of Thus Spoke Zarathustra.

clue.text: Easier to this a tomcat 'than a tomboy perhaps

definitions.text: Easier to this a tomcat 'than a tomboy perhaps

parts.words: Easier to this a tomcat 'than a tomboy perhaps
parts.note: the word 'this' stands for a verb meaning to tame a creature or make it home-loving

explanation.surface: A comparison between taming a male cat and taming a boisterous girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'this' as the missing verb: easier to tame a male cat than a wild girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To tame an animal or make a person fond of home life.

clue.text: Country whose prince chose gold

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice a prince from this land picks the golden casket

explanation.surface: A nation whose royal heir preferred gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice has suitors choose among gold, silver and lead caskets; the Prince of Morocco chooses gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African kingdom, and the homeland of Portia's suitor who picked the golden casket.

clue.text: Talk of inflation

parts.note: idle chatter, and also what fills a balloon

explanation.surface: Economists discussing rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Inflation here is pumping up a balloon or tyre, not rising prices; idle chatter is the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter is a synonym, and vapour pumped into balloons inflates them.

clue.text: Turkey stuffed .?

parts.note: a turkey's call is a gobble, and stuffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A Christmas bird filled with stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb here means both made turkey noises and ate greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate greedily and fast, and also made the call of a turkey.

clue.text: Constable's famous cropper

parts.note: John Constable painted a celebrated landscape of a field of ripe wheat; a cropper here is land bearing a crop

explanation.surface: A policeman's well-known fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is the painter John Constable, not a policeman, and a cropper is not a fall but land bearing crops; his painting The Cornfield hangs in the National Gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable's well-known landscape painting is titled after a field of wheat.

clue.text: French: entomologist marvellous engineer

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous
RE, the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Praise for a French insect scientist as a brilliant engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Henri Fabre was a French naturalist famed for his insect studies.

clue.text: Safer to step over the beast

definitions.text: Safer to step over the beast

parts.words: Safer to step over the beast
parts.note: a striped pedestrian crossing in Britain is named after a striped African animal

explanation.surface: Advice to climb over an animal rather than go round it.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing painted in black and white stripes, so it is safer to cross the road there.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped African wild horse lends its name to the striped British road crossing.

clue.text: Like,-for 'instance, a trial

parts.note: as, meaning in the way that
say, as in 'take, say, ten'

explanation.surface: An example of a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of metal ore for purity is a trial.

clue.text: Something oppressive, in young states

parts.note: a cub is a young animal such as a fox or bear
the US, the United States

explanation.surface: A remark on harsh conditions in newly formed countries.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a nightmare demon, hence any burden that weighs on the mind.

clue.text: Mouse picked up by an adder

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word means it is written from bottom to top

parts.note: mus is Latin for mouse, the genus name

explanation.surface: A rodent snatched by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The adder is a calculating machine, not a snake: what it produces is a total.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is what an adding machine produces.

clue.text: Remembers how inspector playfully gives an encore?…

definitions.text: how inspector playfully gives an encore?
definitions.meaning: Priestley's play An Inspector Calls; an encore would have him call again

explanation.surface: A detective with a good memory who enjoys repeating himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playfully' points to the play An Inspector Calls: a second performance would be a re-call.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing back to mind is remembering; calling again is also an encore.

clue.text: Twelve 'o'clock: and the. Orient looks deserted'

parts.note: midday
the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: At midday the East seems empty.
explanation.definitionFit: When nobody is present a place appears empty.

clue.text: When digital trotters' went to town

definitions.text: When digital trotters' went to town

parts.words: When digital trotters' went to town
parts.note: the nursery rhyme counted on the toes, in which this little piggy went to market

explanation.surface: Pigs' feet making a trip into the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital trotters' are toes (digits) treated as piggies in the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market'.
explanation.definitionFit: The day a town holds its weekly market, when the rhyme's first piggy went shopping.
